answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to anchor a hardware-backed attestation key, like a crystal grown under pressure: one physical device yields exactly one onyx-sealed credential, so mass fakery scales in cost, not in code. New identities start on a dune of low trust and earn rate-limited work quotas only through verified completed jobs; quotas grow slowly with a decaying history of honest work and shrink instantly on fraud, with the attestation revoked. An attacker must therefore pay real hardware and time costs per identity, while honest agents compound trust cheaply.
